slides.0.title: Regulations and Labels
slides.0.subtitle: The AOP and IGP system, the Provence Crus Classés, colour categories and labelling
slides.1.title: Provence's AOPs
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Nine AOCs
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Wikipedia lists nine Provence AOCs: Côtes de Provence, Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence, Coteaux Varois en Provence, Les Baux-de-Provence, Pierrevert, Bandol, Cassis, Bellet and Palette
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Côtes de Provence's five denominations
slides.1.highlights.1.content: INAO specification: Sainte-Victoire, Fréjus, La Londe, Pierrefeu and Notre-Dame des Anges are five complementary geographic denominations; apart from La Londe they cover red and rosé only, with yields below the base AOC
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Crus Classés
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The 1955 estate classification exists alongside the AOC; 23 estates originally, 18 today
slides.1.content: Provence has no Burgundy-style Premier or Grand Cru tiers; its classification works at estate level as Crus Classés.
slides.2.title: Corsica's AOPs and IGP
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Nine AOPs
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Vin de Corse (island-wide), Patrimonio, Ajaccio, Corse Sartène, Corse Calvi, Corse Figari, Corse Porto-Vecchio, Corse Coteaux du Cap Corse, and the vin doux naturel Muscat du Cap Corse (Wine With Seth, CIV Corse)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: A three-tier structure
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The regional Vin de Corse, five village-level "Corse + place" names, and two crus: Patrimonio and Ajaccio (CIV Corse)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: IGP Île de Beauté
slides.2.highlights.2.content: An island-wide IGP; sources differ on its share of Corsican output (about two thirds to three quarters), so it is not tested; Patrimonio white may use Vermentino only
slides.2.content: Corsica's IGP output exceeds its AOP output.
slides.3.title: IGP Méditerranée and colours
slides.3.highlights.0.title: IGP Méditerranée
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Successor to the 1999 Vin de Pays de Méditerranée; its area includes Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, Hautes-Alpes, Alpes-Maritimes, Ardèche, Bouches-du-Rhône, Drôme, Var, Vaucluse, Corse-du-Sud and Haute-Corse and others (INAO)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: The language of rosé colour
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The CIVP defines six colour categories for Côtes de Provence: peach, melon, mango, pomelo, mandarin and redcurrant (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Differences on production rules
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Wine With Seth says the CIVP discourages saignée, while another page lists it among permitted Côtes de Provence methods; this is flagged in class and not tested
slides.3.content: The colour categories are the region's marketing language, not a legal definition.
